title: Alexandrov star topology on the face poset
body_html:
Alexandrov star topology

For each cell $E$, the open star

$$\mathrm{star}(E) := \{F \in [\![X]\!] : E \le F\}$$

is the up-set at $E$ in the face poset. The Alexandrov topology on $[\![X]\!]$ takes a set to be open iff it is up-closed under the face relation — equivalently, iff it is a union of stars.

Signatures

The star and its membership rewrite:

```lean def AbstractCellComplex.star (E : X) : Set X := {F | E ≤ F}

@[simp] theorem mem_star {E F : X} : F ∈ star E ↔ E ≤ F := Iff.rfl

theorem self_mem_star (E : X) : E ∈ star E := le_refl E ```

The topological-space instance is scoped, i.e. only active inside open AbstractCellComplex, so it does not silently clash with any other topology one might place on X:

lean scoped instance : TopologicalSpace X where IsOpen U := ∀ ⦃E : X⦄, E ∈ U → star E ⊆ U isOpen_univ := ... isOpen_inter := ... isOpen_sUnion := ...

Each star E is open in this topology:

lean theorem isOpen_star (E : X) : IsOpen (star E) := fun _ hE _ hF => le_trans hE hF

Why star topology

The Alexandrov star topology is the "right" topology for making sheaves/cosheaves on a cell complex behave like sheaves/cosheaves on a space:

  • stars form an open basis;
  • $\mathrm{star}(E)$ is the smallest open containing $E$;
  • the value of a sheaf on $\mathrm{star}(E)$ is exactly its stalk at $E$ — the Alexandrov-star sheaf condition.

See Sheaves and cosheaves on X as functor categories for how this underpins the definition of Sheaf and Cosheaf on $[\![X]\!]$.
